data.note: re-export running.live_runs from the gates package

data.text:
Is live_runs a public name of services.gates that belongs on the package, and does re-exporting it alone clear the failing test?
Adding live_runs to the .running import in services/gates/__init__.py clears test_every_public_definition_an_area_makes_is_the_same_object_on_the_package[gates], with no other public name missing.
The test walks every public def of each area and compares it with the package attribute; live_runs is the only public def in running.py the package does not import, and services/leasebreak.py already calls it across a module boundary (RUN.live_runs), so it is public rather than a private helper.

data.body:
Fixes bug B0f41a2f1d6: On fix-B-main-red-gates-live-runs-not-exported the ci and unit_tests gates each measured 48 of 48 failures still failing on the base (unmeasured 0), but baseline.auto.accepted stayed false with why 'the import reach cannot be told (a hub module changed: ddflow.services.gates (150 importing files))'. A full suite ran and every failure was measured on a clean base, so reach is not needed to attribute them. The complete then fell through to policy:complete_unavailable as complete.force (Q2eac508789, forced true), and with that policy off the same item would be refused.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B0f41a2f1d6 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B0f41a2f1d6 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B0f41a2f1d6: accept_baseline_red declines a fully measured baseline-red run when a hub module changed
